title: A shared registry conversation: proposal to Dravet Syndrome Foundation

sentences.text: At The Cute Syndrome Foundation, we support families affected by SCN8A-related disorders; your foundation supports families affected by SCN1A-related disorders, including Dravet syndrome.
Both genes help nerve cells send electrical signals through sodium channels.
The atlas also infers similar symptoms, but that connection has confidence 0.49, below 0.5—not proof that families’ needs are identical.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The International SCN8A Registry collects families’ medical and genetic information, and Citizen Health lists SCN8A among its communities.
Simons Searchlight includes SCN1A families; adapting its approach for SCN8A is a possibility to explore, not confirmed access.
We propose comparing registry questions and family-facing information before considering anything larger.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please help check whether severe temper tantrums, esophoria and focal tonic seizures occur in SCN1A families, and review the additional symptom gaps flagged for adapting Searchlight.
The SCN1A loss-of-function connection is contested in the atlas because some non-Dravet variants increase function; we should read both sides of the evidence.
SCN8A also has variants that increase or reduce function, so shared biology should not mean assuming every variant behaves alike.
Before proceeding, let’s check the wider resource landscape and individual variant effects using the questions below.
Let’s jointly send SLC6A1 Connect one short inquiry asking whether Simons Searchlight could include SCN8A-related disorders and what adaptations would be needed.
What patient organisations, registries, trials and research groups exist for SCN8A-related disorders beyond those verified here?
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired or loss of function—in other words, increasing activity, impairing it or reducing function?
I’m writing on behalf of The Cute Syndrome Foundation to propose a small collaboration.
Could we jointly ask SLC6A1 Connect about possible SCN8A inclusion in Simons Searchlight?
We would like to explore useful overlap while checking symptom differences and variant-specific evidence.
Would you be willing to help shape that inquiry this month?
[Your name], on behalf of The Cute Syndrome Foundation
